limitations: Three samples are observations, not a statistical worst-case bound.
Python-first then native-second order may bias cache/thermal state; no favorable sample selection.
Kernel process high-water includes previous cases, not isolated per-case memory peaks.
64-anchor scaled recursive timing has projected HOLD even with MOVE gate; it is not a high-switching state throughput certificate.
Independent fixed unscaled H200 full-trace test exercises both contexts and nonzero movement without changing timing matrix.
The full caller is frozen Python only; native injection exists only in lab-only recurrence.
C ABI raw pointers/checked reuse assume real declared buffers; arbitrary hostile pointers are not memory safe.
Receipt/binary checks detect drift; same-user/compromised-compiler provenance and OS sandboxing are not claimed.
One artifact fd/handle is retained per process; current fenv queried without changing caller settings.
CPU/wall, native allocator retention, actual input/output/host capacity remain unproved.
